 Order

The petitioner has challenged a charge sheet bearing No.38/2017 dated 21.08.2017 filed for the offences punishable under Sections 173, 174, 179, 201, 279, 338, 304A of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (for short, 'IPC') and Sections 181 and 187 of the Indian Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short,
'Act, 1988') and C.C. No.484/2017 registered against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences, which is pending on the file of Civil Judge (Jr. Dn.) and JMFC., Narasimharajapura.
2.

A case in Crime No.1/2017 was registered by the respondent No.2 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337, 304A of IPC and Section 187 of the Act, 1988 before the Additional Civil Judge (Jr. Dn.) and JMFC., Narasimharajapura, Chikkamagalur District.
3. The petitioner claims to be the owner of a goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-18-A-1078.
He NC: 2023:KHC:40889 claimed that on 10.01.2017, the driver - Mr. Prakash had taken the vehicle to a farm at K. Kanabur to transport a load of plantains.

On the same day, at about 8 p.m., the driver came back with the vehicle for a second load and left K.Kanabur to N.R. Pura at 10.30 p.m. and reached N.R. Pura at 11 p.m. and returned to K. Kanabur at 11.30 p.m.
There were four labourers who were engaged in the vehicle and the father of the petitioner named Mr. Poulose accompanied the said labourers.
On their way, the driver and Mr. Anil and Mr. Poulose saw an accident involving a two wheeler and they learnt that the pillion rider had succumbed to the injuries.
They saw a police vehicle at the spot.
On 15.01.2017, the vehicle belonging to the petitioner was again transporting a load of plantains and left Muthinakoppa towards Mangaluru.
When it reached Kalanayakanakatte at about 11 p.m., the vehicle hit a tree on the left side of the road and toppled and fell into a ditch.
The driver was shifted to Koppa Taluk hospital for treatment and he was discharged the next day.
The accident was witnessed by a resident of NC: 2023:KHC:40889 Kalanayakanakatte.
Thereafter, the petitioner went to the spot of the accident and got the vehicle extracted from the ditch.
The load of plantains in the vehicle of the petitioner was shifted to another vehicle bearing registration No.KA- 18-C-0602 owned by Mr.Bebi, son of Mr.Varghese.
The damaged vehicle of the petitioner was towed from Kalanayakanakatte to N.R. Pura Police Station.

On 16.01.2017, the respondent No.2 / Circle Inspector stopped the vehicle at B.H. Kaimara and enquired how the vehicle met with an accident,
which was explained.
The respondent No.2 allowed the vehicle to move further.
When the vehicle had moved 2 Kms. away from B.H. Kaimara, the Circle Inspector called the petitioner and asked him to wait for him.
Later, he directed the petitioner to leave the damaged vehicle of the petitioner at the Police Station.
Though the petitioner claimed that it was a self accident, yet the respondent No.2 did not assign any reason for keeping the vehicle at the Police Station.
Accordingly, the petitioner left the vehicle at the Station.

Since no steps were taken by the respondent No.2 for NC:
2023:KHC:40889 more than 15 days and the battery and stepney from the vehicle were stolen, the petitioner submitted a complaint to the Superintendent of Police on 30.01.2017.

The Circle Inspector called the petitioner and asked him to sign a few blank papers and took two photographs Eldhose M P vs State Of Karnataka on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152364165/
2 of the vehicle with the petitioner on 10.02.2017 under the guise of releasing it as it was not involved in any accident.

sentences.text: However, the respondent No.2 used the blank signed papers to create documents to seem as if the accident dated 10.01.2017 was caused by the vehicle bearing registration No.KA-18- A-1078 belonging to the petitioner.

The petitioner contends that contrarily in Crime No.1/2017 registered in respect of the accident that happened on 10.01.2017, it was stated that a person named Mr.Eldo was riding a vehicle bearing No.KA-18-EC-2637 and an unknown pick up vehicle dashed against it, as a result of which the pillion rider died at the spot.
It was also stated therein that the accident happened at Handiguni cross, N.R. Pura.
The petitioner contends that the blank papers signed by him were used by respondent No.2 to create seizure NC: 2023:KHC:40889 mahazar of his vehicle and other documents to file a charge sheet.

The petitioner allegedly brought this to the notice of the Superintendent of Police and Director General of Police and informed them about the high handed act of the respondent No.2 in implicating his vehicle.

The petitioner thereafter approached the Superintendent of Police who conducted an enquiry by tracking the movement of the petitioner from the mobile towers, the call details of the petitioner, witnesses and others involved.

He also enquired the witnesses Mr. Ramesh and Mr.O.M. Mathai and ascertained their locations from the mobile towers and found that they were not present on 10.01.2017 at the time and place of the accident.

The Superintendent of Police therefore, issued an endorsement dated 20.07.2017 stating that there was no evidence to state that the vehicle of the petitioner was involved in the accident dated 10.01.2017 and therefore, handed over the vehicle to the petitioner.
He also directed the respondent No.2 / Investigating Officer to investigate and find out the vehicle involved in the accident dated 10.01.2017.
Despite this, respondent No.2 filed a charge sheet on 21.08.2017 alleging that the vehicle of the petitioner was responsible for the accidental death of a pillion rider - Mr. Nataraj on 10.01.2017.
The petitioner is therefore before this Court challenging the charge sheet filed.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that a Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-18-EC-2637 was ridden by a person named Mr.K.T. Eldo and he was cited as CW.15 in the charge sheet.
However, the vehicle was later changed to an Apache Bike bearing registration No.KA-15-K-9235 and Mr.K.T. Eldo was arraigned as accused No.2 in the charge sheet.
The petitioner was charge sheeted as accused No.1 being the driver of the goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-18-A-1078.
The petitioner therefore contends that the respondent No.2 was instrumental in swapping the two wheeler and also falsely implicating the vehicle belonging to the petitioner.
Hence, he prays that the charge sheet be quashed.

This Court noticed that even after the endorsement dated 20.07.2017 issued by the Superintendent of Police, no conscious effort was made either by the respondent No.2 or his superiors to ascertain the involvement of the goods vehicle bearing registration KA-18-A-1078.

The learned High Court Government Pleader was therefore directed in terms of the order of this Court dated 23.08.2023 to secure instructions whether the complaint of the petitioner dated 30.01.2017 to the Superintendent of Police was investigated or not and whether the endorsement dated 20.07.2017 was issued by him or not.

The learned High Court Government Pleader submitted that Eldhose M P vs State Of Karnataka on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152364165/
3 there was no clear material to show that the complaint of the petitioner dated 30.01.2017 was looked into or not but affirmed that the endorsement dated 20.07.2017 was issued by the Superintendent of Police.

entities.text: Eldhose M P vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court therefore impressed upon the State Public Prosecutor as to what action would be taken on the complaint of the petitioner.

The learned State Public Prosecutor submitted that the complaint of the petitioner NC: 2023:KHC:40889 would be looked into by the incumbent Superintendent of Police and a report would be placed before this Court at the earliest.

Following this, a report is submitted by the Superintendent of Police, Chikkamagaluru District, stating that the vehicle belonging to the petitioner bearing registration No.KA-18-A-1078 is not involved in the accident dated 10.01.2017 and that it is wrongly implicated.

Therefore, nothing remains to be considered in this petition and this is a clear case of respondent No.2 abusing his power and implicating the vehicle belonging to the petitioner so as to help the claimants of the deceased in the accident to claim compensation.
The charge sheet filed therefore, is liable to be quashed.

6. In that view of the matter, this petition is allowed and the charge sheet bearing No.38/2017 dated 21.08.2017 filed by the respondent No.2 and proceedings in C.C. No.484/2017 pending on the file of Civil Judge (Jr. Dn.) and JMFC., Narasimharajapura, for the offences punishable under Sections 173, 174, 179, 201, 279, 338,
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40889 304A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 181 and 187 of the Indian Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 qua the petitioner/accused No.1 are quashed.

7. The learned State Public Prosecutor has informed the Court that the officer who filed the charge sheet against the petitioner has retired from service but his retirement benefits are not yet released.

In that view of the matter, an enquiry shall be held against the officer concerned by the Superintendent of Police, Chikkamagaluru District, who shall submit a report to this Court about the action taken against the concerned officer.
In order to keep track of the action that may be initiated, list this petition on 29.11.2023.
